item.title: The Summer Job That Ended In Tragedy
item.description:
When 17-year-old Lisa Holm finished her shift at a café in Blomberg, Sweden, she should have been heading home. Instead, she vanished, and her disappearance quickly triggered a massive search involving police, volunteers, and communities across the country.
Days later, investigators found Lisa dead near the area where she had been working, and the case soon focused on a local man whose DNA and other evidence linked him to the crime. The murder shocked Sweden because it began with something so ordinary: a teenager finishing work and expecting to go home.
Do you think cases like Lisa’s feel especially disturbing because they begin during such an ordinary everyday moment?
